gloss: to start walking; to set off on foot

definitions.gloss: to start walking; to set off on foot
definitions.explanation: To begin walking after standing still, or to set out toward somewhere. Also used of a baby taking its first steps.

examples.japanese: ⟦{黙|だま}って→黙る：02287_damaru⟧{歩|ある}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: He started walking without a word.

examples.japanese: ⟦{信号|しんごう}→信号：03258_shingou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{青|あお}→青：02841_ao⟧になった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{歩|ある}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The light turned green, so I started walking.

examples.japanese: ⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{一歳|いっさい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{誕生日|たんじょうび}→誕生日：02910_tanjoubi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{歩|ある}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: My daughter started walking just before her first birthday.
I was waiting for the rain to stop, but it never let up, so I put up my umbrella and set off.

notes:
ASPECT: 〜⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ marks the onset of the motion, so {歩|ある}き{出|だ}す normally appears in the past ({歩|ある}き{出|だ}した) or in て-form leading into what happened next. For walking that is under way, use ⟦{歩|ある}いている→歩く：00538_aruku⟧.

FORMS:
Compound verb: ⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (to walk) + ⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to begin). Figuratively it can describe a project or a life finally getting under way: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{歩|ある}き{出|だ}す (to set out on a new path).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{走|はし}り{出|だ}す→走り出す：06679_hashiridasu⟧: to start running — the same pattern with a faster motion
- ⟦{歩|ある}き→歩く：00538_aruku⟧{始|はじ}める: to begin walking — neutral, without the sense of abruptness
- ⟦{出発|しゅっぱつ}する→出発する：01832_shuppatsusuru⟧: to depart — about leaving for a destination, by any means of travel
